relevance_note: Case report of a newborn with ATS carrying a homozygous SLC2A10 variant: 'a pathogenic c.243C>G (p.Ser81Arg) homozygous variant'.
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON. No table transcription by script. Scope: the index newborn ('patient'); the father, paternal grandmother and paternal aunt (described in relation to the patient: father with features 'suggestive of an ATS carrier', grandmother and aunt 'also positive for ATS'). The mother is described only as a healthy primigravida with thalassemia and gestational diabetes, neither tested nor affected, so she gets no row. Four previously published individuals mentioned in the Introduction/Discussion with an individual-level fact were included under the v4 rule: ref [1] (10-year-old female), ref [17] (epilepsy), ref [16] (cerebral artery tortuosity, migraine), ref [5] (pulmonary hypertension, venous tortuosity). Table 1 (previously published SLC2A10 mutations) is a catalogue of genotypes/variants with references, not of identified patients (no patient label, sex, age or feature), so no rows were created from it; likewise the group statements (14 Qatari patients, seven Saudi cases, 48 Riyadh/Doha patients, adult cases [5-7], ref [7] case previously diagnosed as EDS with no further individual fact) gave no rows. No relative was genotyped; inheritance is 'not reported' and no variant rows exist for relatives. Age at last evaluation for the patient taken as the age at presentation ('four-day-old'); follow-up visits after discharge are reported without an age. Vital status left 'not reported' (follow-up 'no active issues' but alive status not stated explicitly). Checklist 'respiratory distress or insufficiency' left 'not reported' for the patient: the paper says 'not in respiratory distress' but does not address insufficiency (narrow absence does not exclude a composite item); the narrower phenotypic_features row 'respiratory distress' is excluded. 'no pulmonary valve stenosis' and 'no left or right ventricular outflow tract obstruction' were not used for the pulmonary artery stenosis or aortic stenosis checklist items (different structures). 'Ultrasound examinations of the abdomen, head, and hip joints appeared healthy' is a normal examination as a whole and is recorded as written, excluding nothing more specific. Contradictions/oddities: the echocardiogram reports a 'double aortic arch' while CT angiography reports 'a left-sided aortic arch'; the echo lists both 'patent foramen ovale' and 'no septal defect'; parents are called 'healthy' but the father is said to have dysmorphic features suggestive of an ATS carrier; the abstract says the grandmother and aunt 'were also positive for ATS' while the case text says only that they 'also had such appearances' (carrier-like features) without severe cardiovascular complications, and no testing is reported. The 'no pulmonary artery drainage' echo finding is recorded as written; its meaning is unclear. The relatives' 'such appearances' refers back to the father's features (slim, tall, dysmorphic face).
